text: From React interface to live, AI-powered serverless app
React + Vite   /   Express MVC   /   OpenAI-compatible API   /   Vercel
Project presentation for the Serverless AI Chatbot. The live app root URL is inferred from the user-supplied health endpoint; the health endpoint is listed separately on the final slide.
A complete chat experience, from browser to model
The project pairs a responsive React client with a Node.js API that runs as Vercel serverless functions.
A public chatbot with conversation controls, protected server-side AI credentials, and a deployable API.
Project implementation details summarized from the repository: https://github.com/85kartik/serverless-AI-chatbot
One request travels through four clear layers
The browser sends chat history to the app API; the AI provider response returns through the same path.
The provider key stays on the server; it is never bundled into the React app.

Architecture reflects the project entry points and server code. Vercel function configuration and routing are defined in the root vercel.json. See https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json
MVC keeps each responsibility in its place
The repository separates the chat interface, request handling, and AI-provider work.
Calls the AI provider with a reusable system prompt and selected model.
Validates the request, checks message history, and returns an HTTP response.
Renders chat, navigation, loading, error states, and conversation controls.

Files are based on the repository structure. This is a lightweight MVC-style separation: the React app is the view, the Express controller and routes handle requests, and the AI service/config layer acts as the model integration.
A ChatGPT-inspired interface includes useful controls for starting, revisiting, and clearing chats.
I can help you design it step by step.
Browse saved chats and open the panel again after collapsing it.
Start fresh or remove a conversation with clear controls.
Use the chat on desktop or a narrow mobile screen.
Loading indicator, recoverable errors, and automatic scroll.
The conversation mockup is a conceptual depiction of implemented chat UI elements and is not a screenshot of the live app.
From typed message to assistant reply
Each request is validated and assembled on the server before the provider is called.
Client rejects blank input and sends current conversation history.
Controller checks roles, message lengths, and history limits.
AI service adds the reusable system instruction.
Official OpenAI SDK requests a chat completion.
API sends assistant text; UI appends it and scrolls to latest.
Request flow described from the frontend chat service, Express chat controller, and server/services/aiService.js implementation.
Protect credentials and make failures understandable
Practical guardrails cover browser input, API access, and provider failures.
The provider API key is read from server environment variables.
Payload size and conversation history are bounded; rate limiting is configured.
CORS and security headers help control who can call the API.
Invalid JSON, oversized messages, provider quota, and connection errors map to clear responses.
Server logs capture error metadata without printing prompts or secrets.
Chat data remains in browser storage, with retry and clear-chat paths.
Set OPENAI_API_KEY in Vercel project settings; never place it in client code.

Security controls are described based on project code. Rate limiting uses process memory, which can reset between serverless invocations; a shared persistent limiter would be needed for stronger production enforcement. Do not add real API credentials to source control.
GitHub to Vercel, with the API in the same project
The root configuration builds the Vite client and routes serverless endpoints from the root api directory.
Vercel functions must live in the root /api directory to match the configured function patterns.

Deployment sequence corresponds to the root vercel.json: buildCommand npm run build, outputDirectory client/dist, function patterns api/chat.js and api/health.js, with SPA fallback rewrite. Vercel configuration docs: https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json. GitHub repo: https://github.com/85kartik/serverless-AI-chatbot
Ship a working baseline, then strengthen it
The project demonstrates an end-to-end AI feature and leaves a clear path for production improvements.
React UI → Express controller → AI provider
Static frontend and API functions on one Vercel project
History, new chat, clear, loading, errors, mobile layout
Use shared storage such as Redis across function instances
Add authentication and durable conversation storage
Return tokens incrementally for faster perceived response
The deployment is a strong assignment-ready foundation; future changes can improve scale and personalization.

Current-state and future-work summary. The existing rate limiter uses in-memory state and therefore should be replaced with shared storage if strict global limits are needed across serverless instances.
